payload.explanation: During place_u_orange's final descent to the placement frame (wall_ns ~1791492525.0-525.3e9), stat_base1 fired at a 5.66mm displacement (threshold 5mm, agent-chosen since base1 has no contract) and stat_u_brown fired at 12.5mm (threshold 10mm, derived from u_brown's own raw_spec.tolerances.position_m). get_evidence over the window shows base1's z rising from 0.02241m to a peak 0.02909m with its orientation tilting (quaternion x-component spiking to 0.043) and u_brown's z rising from 0.04335m to a peak 0.05581m with similar transient tilt, both synchronized with u_orange's z dropping from ~0.128m to ~0.048m as it was lowered into base1's slot. This is consistent with the carried u_orange part grazing/contacting base1 and transmitting a jolt to the adjacent already-seated u_brown as it was lowered past them -- the real contact channel this task's ACM configuration permits (carried-part-vs-bystander/fixture). Both objects settled back close to their original poses by end_step (base1 final residual ~2.6mm from pre-step pose, u_brown final residual ~1.9mm, both consistent with the executor's own claim_detail reporting u_brown_disturbance_m=0.00105 at closure). I am flagging this as non_conformant rather than accepting the recovered end-state because the undisturbed-objects requirement is an invariant that must hold throughout the step, not only at its close, and a measurable contact-induced displacement did occur mid-step. The executor's end_step claim only reports u_brown's final residual and does not mention base1 at all, so this finding would otherwise go unrecorded. place_u_orange's own effects (u_orange seated at u_orange_placement, position_error 0.0024m within the 0.02m tolerance; grasp confirmed by force_threshold contact at pick with width 0.0206m vs 0.02m expected; grasp retention monitor slip_u_orange never fired across the whole hold) are otherwise conformant.

payload.explanation: stat_hex_red fired at a 49.99mm displacement, threshold 5mm. get_evidence over the surrounding window shows hex_red's pose held fixed at (0.11455,0.03938,0.07488) for many samples, then abruptly stepped to (0.06455,0.03938,0.07488) -- a clean 0.05m shift along world X only, with y, z and orientation all unchanged to the sub-millimeter -- and then held fixed at the new pose for the remainder of the window. This step (pick_line_green) only names line_green in object_ids, and get_evidence confirms line_green itself never moved during this window (it had not yet been grasped). get_evidence on the tcp frame over the same window shows the arm stationary at (0.815,-0.246,0.233), nowhere near hex_red's location, so this is not an arm-strike or a carried-part contact -- no carried part was in motion near hex_red at all. The clean axis-aligned, zero-rotation step (rather than a slide, tip, or bounce) is not consistent with a physical collision signature; I cannot determine the physical mechanism from available evidence and am recording this as an unexplained scene event (see record_observation) rather than asserting a cause. Regardless of mechanism, hex_red is a bystander under continuous protection -- the instruction states any movement of one, at any time, is a disturbance -- and it moved, so this is non_conformant. No other clause for this step is affected; line_green itself was not yet acted on at the time of this fire.

payload.explanation: This is the run's final end-state verdict. All four parts were independently measured by me via query_snapshot against their published placement frames at run end: u_brown 2.2mm from u_brown_placement (tol 10mm), u_orange 2.0mm from u_orange_placement (tol 20mm), line_green 6.6mm from line_green_placement (tol 15mm), inverted_u_yellow 1.2mm from inverted_u_yellow_placement (tol 12mm) -- all seated conformant, and base1 was never picked and its net residual displacement from its pre-run pose is under 1mm (recovered). Grasp retention (relative_frame monitors) never fired across any of the four holds, and every grasp's effort/width/lift-height effects were within their contract thresholds. Two findings were recorded during the run: (1) place_u_orange -- stat_base1 and stat_u_brown fired during u_orange's final descent (5.66mm and 12.5mm transient displacement respectively); evidence showed a contact-induced jolt from the carried u_orange grazing base1/u_brown, with both settling back close to their original poses by end_step. This is a real but RECOVERED invariant violation: it does not stand at run end. (2) pick_line_green -- stat_hex_red fired at a 49.99mm displacement; evidence showed hex_red made a clean, instantaneous 0.05m shift along world X with zero accompanying rotation, while the TCP was stationary and far away and line_green itself had not yet been grasped, so this was not an arm-strike or carried-part contact; I could not establish the physical mechanism and recorded it as an unexplained scene event (observation obs-001-71fd0f41) rather than assert a cause. Querying hex_red at run end shows it remains at the displaced pose (0.0645, 0.0394, 0.0749) -- identical to its post-fire position -- with no subsequent step ever acting on it (it is not among this task's four parts). This is a STANDING, uncorrected violation of the continuous undisturbed-bystander requirement at run end. Per the verdict rules, a violation still standing at run end makes the run non_conformant regardless of every part's own placement being correct and regardless of the executor's claimed "completed" status (the executor's own end_step/run_ended payloads never reference hex_red at all, since it is not a step object for this task -- the executor could not see this failure). All other bystanders (u_green, inverted_u_brown, hex_blue, base2) were independently confirmed at run end to match their initial reference poses exactly.
